## Correction — `displayMode` is NOT among the keys these registrations read

From the `domain:ui` PM seat, before dispatching this card. The body says:

> the keys those registrations read (`surface`, `processVisibility`, `displayMode`, `floatingConfig`) are declared on `ChatbotSchema`

`displayMode` does not belong in that list, and objectui#7654 — which is parked on `needs-user-decision` for exactly this key — is the one that has it right.

### Measurement

Word-boundary grep for `displayMode` over `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/**` on `origin/main`, tests excluded. **Two hits, both in `renderer.tsx`, neither a read:**

| site | what it is |
| :-- | :-- |
| `renderer.tsx:504` | a designer `inputs` entry — declares the *control* |
| `renderer.tsx:526` | a `defaultProps` entry — *seeds* the value |

There is no `schema.displayMode` or `props.displayMode` consumption anywhere in the package.

**Lit controls, same instrument, same population:** `floatingConfig` 3 hits in `FloatingChatbot.tsx` + 8 in `renderer.tsx`; `surface` across 13 files; `processVisibility` 11 in `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` + 2 in `renderer.tsx`. The instrument reads non-zero, so the zero above is a reading.

The `displayMode` hits in `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx` are a **different key** — a React prop typed `'grid' | 'list'` on a field widget, unrelated to `ChatbotSchema.displayMode` (`'inline' | 'floating'`, `complex.ts:886`).

### Why this matters beyond one wrong parenthetical

The other three keys are genuinely read, so the card's central claim — that two of three registrations have no importable authoring-face type — stands and this card is dispatchable. But `displayMode` is the opposite case: **declared, offered as a designer control, seeded into `defaultProps`, and read by nothing.** Anyone reading this card's list would conclude it is live and carry that into a fix.

⛔ This card does not decide `displayMode`'s fate. objectui#7654 owns it and is parked on a maintainer decision. Whichever interface `displayMode` ends up on, it moves across unchanged.

## ⛔ The dispatch fence this PR was built on was STALE, and that is the seat's error, not the dev seat's

The contract review of PR #7705 (comment to follow on that PR) found it first. Recording it here because the dev seat followed the brief exactly and the brief was wrong.

### What happened

My claim comment and both dispatch briefs said `displayMode` was **"parked on a maintainer decision"** and told the dev to carry it across unchanged because objectui#7654 owned its fate.

**objectui#7654 was ruled at 2026-09-05T02:48:39Z** — comment 5548848737, maintainer verbatim 「同意」, decision batch #44. **Ruling B: retire `displayMode`** — `?: never` tombstone on `ChatbotSchema`, the designer control and the `defaultProps` seed removed. `needs-user-decision` was cleared in the same stroke; the card has read `pm:queue` since.

The first dispatch of this card was killed by a rate limit. When I re-issued the brief after the quota reset — **more than four hours after that ruling** — I copied the fence forward without re-reading the card. The stale sentence then propagated into eight lines across five tree carriers, the changeset, the PR body and the dev report.

### Why it is worse than an ordinary stale read

The ruling cites **this seat's own measurement** as its ground: *"citing discriminator prong 2 (advertised at `CHANGELOG.md:578`, 3.3.0) exactly as the ui seat's 02:32Z measurement at `5548764449` established."*

So the sequence was: I measured `displayMode`, the maintainer ruled on that measurement, and I then dispatched a brief telling a dev the question was still open. ⛔ There is no version of "the base moved under me" that covers this — I am the one who moved it.

### The rule this breaks is the one this seat has been enforcing all day

Every dispatch brief and every review brief issued today carries: **⛔ read the current state of every card and PR you name before writing a tense for it.** Two contract-review REFUSEs earlier today were issued on exactly that defect in other seats' work. This is the same defect in mine, and it is the fifth instance I have recorded today of ruling or briefing from material I had not re-read.

⭐ The instruction is not enough on its own. Re-issuing a brief after an interruption is the specific moment it fails, because the brief *looks* already-verified. Any brief re-sent after a gap gets its cards re-read first — that is the concrete change, and it goes into this seat's check-in.

### What this changes for PR #7705

Nothing about the ruled shape (one interface per registration stands, #6169). What changes:

- Every `displayMode` tense in the tree, the changeset and the PR body must read **ruled B**, not parked.
- `displayMode` still stays **untouched in this PR** — but for a different reason. Not "pending a decision": the decision exists and its execution is **#7654's own PR**, which must tombstone the member on `ChatbotSchema` and strip the control and the seed. This PR must leave that member executable for it.
- Which is why the review's other blocking item follows: moving `displayMode` off `ChatbotSchema` hollows the exact member ruling B names. Option **B — keep both keys on `ChatbotSchema`** — is now not merely the reviewer's preference; it is what leaves the ruling executable as written.

Remediation dispatched with the corrected fence.
